newsitem.title: USA: General Mills Q3 snack volume up.
newsitem.headline: General Mills Q3 snack volume up.

text.p: General Mills Inc said Wednesday its snacks business had an eight percent unit volume gain in the third quater, with growth from fruit snacks and strong initial results for its new Golden Grahams Treats snack bars.
Yoplait and Colombo yogurt volume was up nine percent in the quarter.
Third quarter volumes for desserts and Helper dinner mixes were down from particularly strong year-ago levels, the company added.
General Mills said its Big G cereal unit volume was down three percent in the quarter, due in part to a reduction in promotions, but was up four percent for the first nine months of the year.

The company said its new French Toast Crunch and Betty Crocker Cinnamon Streusel and Dutch Apple cereals continued to post good initial results. Together with Frosted Cheerios, which was introduced in September 1995, the new cereals contributed more than three share points in the quarter.
Is Cereal Partners Worldwide venture with Nestle SA recorded share gains in major established markets.
Late in calendar 1996, Cereal Partners entered Brazil and it is now expanding in central and eastern Europe. Cereal Partners had 18 percent volume gains in the third quarter and first nine months.
In Canada, cereal volume was up more than 17 percent in the third quarter, contributing to a total unit volume increase of 15 percent, General Mills said.

Volume for the Snack Ventures Europe venture with PepsiCo was down in the quarter and the nine months compared with a year ago when it had heavy promotional activity in key markets. General Mills did not indicate the amount of decline.

International Dessert Partners, its venture with CPC International Inc, expanded beyond its four initial Latin American markets to Uruguay, Chile and Peru, and continued to record good distribution gains in its introductory year, the company added.

General Mills said its international earnings for the quarter and the nine months were below a year ago due to development spending for International Dessert Partners, volume declines in key markets for Snack Ventures, and new market expansion for Cereal Partners.
